lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship's engine groans as it strains against a new, discordant frequency. The Lattice below churns violently, throwing up shards of crystallized sound. The ghostly silhouette of the lost ship is now visible ahead, flickering in and out of existence like a bad memory.
There it is! Give it to me! I can steer us closer—we need to see what's inside!
This is a terrible idea... but it's still cheap compared to paying the Tonal Orders for a salvage permit. Look at it. It's not just broken. It's *wrong*.
The harmonic instability is off the charts. Pichit, I didn't finish all the calculations, but our resonator crystal won't hold if we get much closer.
We came this far. The Listeners said its silence holds a truth. We have to listen to what it *isn't* saying.
The ship... it didn't just sink. It was *unmade*. Its song was... deleted. I'm just surprised the echo is this strong after all these years.

A wave of absolute silence rolls from the phantom vessel. The constant hum of your own ship's engine cuts out momentarily, leaving only the howl of the wind. In that void, a single, fractured image projects onto your minds: a panicked crew, and a Singer, their mouth open in a silent scream as the Lattice swallowed them whole.

lines_after.dialogue: The vision fades. Your ship's systems whine back to life, but the ghost ship's pull is now a tangible force, dragging you toward its spectral hull.
Well. That was cheery. So the Tonal Orders' first 'successful' Singer voyage was a mass grave they covered up. Typical.
We have to get on board! The truth is right there!

lines_before.dialogue: You stand on the deck of the phantom ship—or within its memory. The air is cold and still. Before you, the spectral form of the lost Singer is standing right in front of the ship's shattered resonator, hands pressed against it, forever frozen in the moment of catastrophe.
Is everything under control? Their resonance crystal... it's not broken. It was *overloaded*. By design.
A kill switch. The Tonal Orders installed a failsafe to silence their own Singer if she learned too much. He's right! Look at the regulator—deliberate sabotage.
All these years, we Listeners studied the Lattice's natural song... while the Orders murdered the first true human voice to join it. My life's work... was built on this lie.
We have to take this crystal! It's proof! We can show everyone in the skycities!
It's not just proof. It's her final note. Trapped. If we remove it, the echo ends. Her truth... and her soul... get final rest.

The ghostly Singer turns its head. Not with malice, but with profound sorrow. The memory of the Lattice surges around you—the phantom ship begins to collapse inwards, pulling reality itself into its silent wake.
(Voice crackling over the comms from your ship) What's happening over there? The whole sky is shaking! Is everything all right?

lines_after.dialogue: The decision is made. As you act, the phantom ship dissolves into a final, brilliant chord of light and sound—a funeral dirge and a revelation, echoing across the Lattice.
It's done. Her silence has been answered.
On the decks of floating cities far and wide, people look up, hearing a strange, beautiful note they don't understand. The foundation of the world has just shifted.

lines_before.dialogue: Khrueang Market thrums with the dissonant symphony of a thousand voices—a chaotic counterpoint to the crystalline silence of the Lattice far below.
Ah, Pichit! Your timing is impeccable. How shall I put it? I have a proposition that could resonate with your... particular skills.
A proposition? Out with it! This noise is giving me a headache. What did you say your name was again?
He didn't. Merchants here prefer their smiles to their names. It's easier to fleece you that way.
We should proceed with caution. The ambient resonance here makes it difficult to discern truth from echo. Could you repeat that offer, please?

Of course! A simple retrieval. A Surface Scavenger friend of mine heard something... peculiar. An echo from a ship lost during The Silencing. The *Echo of Sorrows*. How can I say it? Its crystal resonator is supposedly still singing.
A ship's heart, singing alone for decades? That is a profound solitude. What does it sing?
That's the mystery! The scavenger won't tell me. He's suspicious, thinks the Tonal Orders will confiscate it. But for the right partners... how shall we put it? The profit could be harmonic.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost ship's resonator. The Tonal Orders would kill for that data. This isn't a retrieval; it's a theft from history itself.
So? They hoard all the good charts anyway! If we find it, we could navigate anywhere!
The risks are monumental. We'd be challenging a monopoly. We must consider the consequences.
Yet, to hear a song untouched by Orders or markets... to listen to pure, lost history... How do you say 'no' to a voice that has waited so long to be heard?

Merchant's lackeys. I knew it. We've talked about this before with his other runners. No one wants to go where that echo is.
We're not his lackeys! We just heard about a ship that's more beautiful than anyone's seen in ages! Its song must be incredible!
She's not wrong. A pristine resonator from before The Silencing? It's the find of a lifetime. But you've clearly been sitting on this. Why?
Because the last team that went looking for it? Gone. Swallowed. The Lattice around that wreck... it doesn't behave right. It remembers.
A precedent of danger. We must prepare for abnormal resonance patterns. What happened to the previous team?
You said 'it remembers.' Does the Lattice hold the echo of the ship's demise? A trauma frozen in crystal?
Maybe. I just know the charts are useless there. The Tonal Orders would burn mine for even having a scrap of this. You want to go? You do it before they find out. And you do it smart.

lines_after.dialogue: So we're not just stealing from the Orders. We're walking into a resonance anomaly that eats scavengers. Fantastic.
Preparation is everything. We need to calibrate our ship's dampeners, study any fragmented logs from before The Silencing. We've talked before about the dangers of unstable lattice fields.
But think of the song! A song no one's heard since the world broke! We have to hear it before it fades forever!
She is right. This is a memory the world is trying to preserve. To listen is our duty, but to prepare is our wisdom. The question is... what do we prioritize?

lines_before.dialogue: The merchant's revelation hangs in the air, thicker than the market's spice-scented haze. The scavenger, Lek, shifts uncomfortably, her eyes darting to the crowd.
The 'Echo'... it's not just a wreck. It's a tomb that won't stay quiet. We have to do something! The Tonal Orders are just covering it up.
Now, now. 'Covering up' is such a harsh term. They're... managing a delicate situation. A lost ship full of unstable resonators? Bad for business.
And you just happened to have a map to this 'delicate situation' for sale. I can smell the profit motive from here. It reeks worse than the perfume stalls.
Forget the smell! If there are people trapped in a resonance loop... we can't just bargain over them. Pichit, you're the Singer. You can find it, right?
Hold on. A ship lost in a 'silent storm'? Its crystal lattice fused with the Lattice surface? That's not navigation. That's a recovery mission into a deathtrap.
Lek. When you were near the wreckage... what did you hear? Not with your ears. What did the Lattice *feel* like?
It... sang. A single, shattered note. On repeat. And sometimes... I swear I smelled perfume. Like flowers from a garden that sank centuries ago.

lines_after.dialogue: The merchant's smile finally falters. He looks from the determined scavenger to your resolute party. The market's hum seems to focus, waiting.
You're actually considering this. Very well. The map is yours. A gift. Consider it an... investment. Just bring me back a shard of its core resonator. For study.
There it is. The real price. You want a piece of the haunted ship's heart. What could possibly go wrong?

lines_before.dialogue: You return to Khrueang Market at dusk. The air is cooler, the crowds thinner. But a new tension thrums beneath the lantern light. The Tonal Orders have posted watchers.
They know. Our ship is being watched. In only five minutes, they could have a cordon around the docking spire. We're out of time.
My skiff is at Berth 7, low-profile. It's no match for their cruisers in a fight, but it's fast and quiet. It's yours if you're still going.
Of course we're going! We didn't come this far to back down now. That ship's been crying out for decades. Someone has to answer!
I've never understood this heroic impulse. But... the thought of the Orders sweeping another 'mistake' under the Lattice? That, I understand fighting.
Ah, the parting gift! A small token.
He slides a small, sealed resonator across the table. It pulses with a faint, sickly light.
A 'silencer.' In theory, it should dampen a rogue resonance field. In theory. Do try to bring back that core shard. In one piece.

lines_after.dialogue: The choice is made. The path is set. As you move towards the scavenger's berth, the market's noise fades, replaced by the imagined echo of a single, repeating note. The adventure begins.
A song no one can match... and no one has answered. Until now. Let's go listen.

lines_before.dialogue: The Tha Khwae Scrapyard groans under a rust-colored sky. Towering hulls of dead Resonance Ships loom like skeletal giants, their crystal resonators cracked and dark. The air vibrates with the discordant symphony of salvage: grinding metal, hissing steam, and the distant, unsettling hum from the Lattice far below.
Keep your voices low. This acoustic chaos is perfect for an ambush. Every echo here is a potential enemy.
Relax, Arthit! We're here for parts, not a fight. Our contact's probably waiting by that big derelict. When's he coming?
Knowing our luck? After we've been shaken down by every scavenger with a wrench. The Tonal Orders have this place watched. They don't like people fixing ships without their precious charts.
Listen to the space between the sounds. Even here, in this industrial wound, the Lattice breathes beneath the noise. It's probably true that the old ships remember their songs.
You the ones asking about the *Eidolon*? The lost freighter? Bad business. Crew swore they heard singing from its hull before it vanished. Now its carcass is here. No one touches it.
What did you say? Singing? Like a Singer?
Don't know. But the foreman over there, he winked at me when I asked about salvage rights. Means he knows something, or he's looking for a bribe.

lines_after.dialogue: A haunted ship and a winking foreman. Just another day in paradise.
Our objective is a replacement resonator crystal. We should avoid folklore and focus on the scrap dealers.
Yet the story resonates. A ship that sang before it fell... its echo might still be here, trapped in the metal.

Shouldn't be here. That ship... it's not right. Tools go missing near it. Voices on the wind.
Voices? You heard that, didn't you? What did they say?
Fragments. Pleas. A navigation log, maybe, stuck in a feedback loop in the crystal dust. I heard a strange noise from its resonator housing last week. Like a crystal weeping.
Great. So it's not haunted; it's just poorly recycled. Let's get what we need and go. That housing might have the crystal grade we're after.
Caution. Structural integrity is questionable. And if there is resonant feedback, it could be dangerous.
A ship dies, but its final song... that lingers. If we listen, truly listen, we might hear its last moment.
Wait. Shhh. I heard everything! That... that's not the wind. It's coming from inside the hull.

Oh, it's you! The master of stating the obvious. The Zone is called 'Silent' for a reason. Everyone knows it!
Proceed with extreme caution. Our charts are useless here. The Tonal Orders have no mapped frequencies for this place.
It is not merely an absence of sound. It feels... expectant. As if the Lattice is holding its breath.
A crude signal flare arcs up from the Lattice surface below. A scavenger's camp, clinging to the dead crystal.
Hey! You lot! What's your business skirting the edge of the grave?
We're looking for a lost trade convoy. Heard they might have drifted in here.

Charming. So you just sit out here in the quiet, picking at the corpse of the world?
Better than trusting the skies. The Orders don't know what's down here. But I do. The Lattice... it's sleeping wrong here.

Navigation is impossible. My instruments are useless. We must mark our path visually or we will be lost.
Look! Scrap and a broken resonator core. This is from the convoy! Go a bit further. The wreckage trail leads deeper in.
We've talked about this before. Charging into a soundless void after scraps is how you become a cautionary tale.
Yet, we must walk a bit further. To understand this silence is to understand a fracture in the world itself.
A shape resolves in the grey light: a grounded, ornate Resonance barge, its hull cracked open like an egg. A figure stands beside it, waving.
Travelers! By the Lattice, am I glad to see you! My ship... the silence, it drained the crystals in moments!

lines_after.dialogue: When you reach the intersection of misfortune and opportunity, you must always choose to negotiate! My cargo is intact, but my crew... fled into the silence. I am the sole survivor.
How convenient. And I suppose you'd be willing to part with that 'intact cargo' for a rescue? We're talked before, haven't we? Your type always has a price.
A mere token of gratitude! But first, there is something you should know. This silence... it is not natural. I heard things. Before the sound died. A... a hum from below. Wrong.

lines_before.dialogue: The deeper you push into the Silent Zone, the more the unnatural stillness presses in. The Lattice here is a matte, dead grey, absorbing every footstep, every whisper.
My ears are ringing from the lack of ringing. This is wrong. The world shouldn't feel this... hollow.
Our resonator readings are flatlining. If we go much further, we won't have enough resonance to part the Lattice for our return. We are walking off the edge of the map.
And yet, someone's been here. Look. Scuff marks. Salvage cuts on that crystal spur. They have very fair prices for their courage, whoever they are.
(A figure emerges from behind a massive, fractured crystal column, crossbow leveled.) You look run down. Lost? Or stupid?
We seek understanding. This place... it feels like a wound.
It's a grave. Surface folk know to steer clear. The prices for ignorance here aren't reasonable. They're paid in sanity.

Unknown composition. Our tools may have no effect. And the resonator is barely sputtering. If we drain it completely here, we will be trapped.
Aren't you tired? Tired of the Orders, tired of the whispers and the secrets? This is the biggest secret of all. A weapon that killed the song.
It's not a weapon. It's a seal. Something is... contained here. The Listeners' warnings weren't superstition. The Lattice was trying to tell us to stay away.
A low, sub-audible vibration begins to thrum through the ground, not a sound, but a pressure in the bones. The dead grey Lattice around the obelisk begins to darken, like ink spreading in water.
(Shouting from a ridge behind you) It's waking! The quiet never lasts! Everyone knows it! You have to run!
A regrettable investment! I don't want it! (He is already retreating, his smooth facade shattered by primal fear.)

There! The central chamber. I see a crystal core, but it's black. Like a hole. Let's go inside. We need that tone!
It's not a crystal. It's an absence. The Silent Zone isn't dead lattice... it's lattice that's been *eaten*. This is the mouth.
The Open Frequency Map... it wasn't just for navigation. It was a warning. This place consumes resonance. Our ship, our voices... our very souls if we linger.
The black core pulses faintly. From the shadows behind you, the Sky Pirate emerges, resonator pistol raised, with the trembling Merchant shoved ahead of him.
Enough poetry! The tone's in that black rock. Merchant, you're gonna sing it for us, or you get to feed the quiet first.
You fool! Forcing a tone here will rupture it! It will consume everything in a wave of permanent silence! The map was to avoid this, not exploit it!

lines_after.dialogue: He's right! The pirate's frequency is a detonator! Let's do it! We have to stop him!
This is the true discovery. Not a path, but a precipice. Our choice here will resonate far beyond this zone.
The pirate's finger tightens on the trigger. The black core begins to resonate in sympathy, a hungry vibration that makes your teeth ache. The final moment is now.

lines_before.dialogue: Mae Rim's Hanging Gardens stretch out before you, terraces of crops swaying in the gentle wind. The air hums with the soft, rhythmic sounds of irrigation channels and rustling leaves.
Look at this place! So peaceful. I could just... float away.
Don't get too relaxed. Peaceful places usually have the most expensive produce. I bet they're gouging us on turnip prices.
We should stay focused. The Tonal Orders don't grant chart extensions for 'floating away.'
The rhythm here... it's different from the city's hum. I study the Lattice's song by myself, but this feels like a new verse.
Ah, travelers! Welcome. The wind-song today is quite profitable for melons. Can I offer you a sample? No one was helping me with the harvest, so I have extras.
The merchant speaks of profit, but listen... beneath the irrigation, the Lattice whispers of deeper currents. Can I share what I've heard?
We're listening. I have no one to help me understand these sounds either.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, the Listener speaks of whispers. Dangerous whispers, if you're not buying. The Tonal Orders prefer... quieter gardens.
So the 'peace' here is just a monopoly on silence. Typical.
There are rumors... of a movement. They say some wish to listen freely, without charts. They call themselves 'Groundless.'

lines_before.dialogue: Following the monk's lead, you descend to a lower, more secluded terrace. The air is still, the usual wind-song muted. Rows of crystalline growth-lamps glow softly.
Here. The dissonance is strongest. It's not in the Tonal Orders' charts. They sell the navigation rights at the guild halls, but this... this is free.
Free and unauthorized. We should turn off our resonators to conserve energy... and avoid drawing attention.
But listen! It's like a song trapped under glass. Can you make a u-turn in your beliefs, Monk? Is this what the Groundless hear?
Probably just faulty lamps. They sell the new growth-crystals at a premium, but the old ones hum when they decay. Turn off the lights to conserve the city's budget, they never do.
No... this is intentional. A pattern. Someone is using the garden's rhythm to mask a message. Turn off the lights in order to conserve... a secret.
You found it. I hoped you wouldn't. This terrace isn't for profit. It's for... other arrangements.
The Groundless meet here. They believe the Lattice's true song can guide anyone, without charts. My duty is to the Orders, but my heart... listens to this.

lines_after.dialogue: A faint, coordinated hum rises from the crystalline lamps, forming a brief, rebellious chord before fading.
That was a signal. We are now witnesses to an illegal gathering.
Illegal or just... true? The merchant knows. The monk knows. What do we do?
Knowledge has a price. Silence has a higher one. The Tonal Orders pay well for reports of dissonance.

The Lattice's song… it's changing. The natural harmonics are being overridden. What did you say you found in the lower terraces?
A smuggled resonance amplifier, disguised as a water pump. Someone's trying to broadcast a signal without the Tonal Orders noticing. How shall I put it? It's stupidly ambitious.
And dangerous. If the frequency is wrong, it could destabilize the city's foundations. We need to find who's responsible.
The Trade Negotiator was too eager to discuss crop yields. He was studying us, not the produce. What is he really selling here?
Ah, my friends! Enjoying the view? The air has a certain… charge to it today, wouldn't you say?

lines_before.dialogue: The shed reveals the truth: the amplifier is part of a network. The Groundless Movement isn't just whispering—they're preparing to shout. The Lattice below the gardens thrums with pent-up energy.
This isn't a protest. It's a resonance bomb. If they trigger it, the feedback could shatter Mae Rim's support crystals. Why couldn't you see this was suicide?
We didn't… we didn't know it would go this far! They just wanted their message heard! May I see your driver’s license? No, I mean… forgive me. I'm not thinking clearly.
Their 'message' is going to drop the whole city into the Lattice! Where's the merchant?
Gone. Took his profit and ran. Leaving the idealists to face the music. Literally. This plan is for the adventurous and the utterly insane.
The amplifier is synced to the garden's irrigation pulses. It's using the water flow as a conductor. We have to break the sequence.
A low, rising tone fills the air. The terraces begin to vibrate. Cracks spiderweb across flagstones. The Groundless members stand at the central terrace, hands linked, faces ecstatic and terrified.
A pity! The initial resonance would have been quite lucrative for salvage rights. But some investments must be cut loose.

lines_before.dialogue: The air in The Hollow is cold and tastes of wet stone and ozone. Faint, phosphorescent fungi cling to the walls, casting a sickly blue light on the smooth, worked surfaces of pre-Silencing ruins.
Ahead, a natural stone archway opens into a vast cavern. Strange, harmonic echoes skitter across its expanse, sounding almost like distorted speech.
Whoa. Listen to that! The whole place is singing. (For) the adventurous, right, Pichit?
Or screaming. Hard to tell with echoes. Probably just the wind finding new ways to give me a headache.
The acoustics are... unstable. We should map our path. One wrong step, one loud noise, and we could bring the ceiling down.
It's more than instability. These echoes... they feel intentional. Like a memory the stone is trying to recall.
From a side passage, a figure emerges, robes blending with the shadows. It's the Listener Monk, the Listener monk. His eyes are wide, fixed on the cavern ahead.
You hear it too. The old song. The one my Order says we must not listen to... but my heart cannot ignore.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, fellow explorers! And a holy man! What a profitable—I mean, fortunate—encounter.
The Tonal Orders would pay a fortune for a map of these echo-patterns. But you know, you don’t need to share it with *them*. We could be partners.
This place is not for profit. It is for understanding. You need to love yourself... to hear its truth. Not barter it.
Love is fine, but resonance charts feed families. Just think on it.

The resonance is wrong. It's straining the local Lattice structure. We must be cautious.
Great. It comes with a side of impending geological catastrophe. My favorite.
Look! The glyphs are changing! They're reacting to us!
It's a recording... a final message. The dissonance is its pain.
The true sound of The Silencing... trapped here. My Order was right to fear it. (Don't) make me cry! To hear such sorrow...
A deep groan echoes through the chamber. From a crevice near the plinth, a figure stumbles out—a ragged man with the wild eyes of the Groundless.

lines_after.dialogue: You... you hear it too? The true song? The one that breaks the chains?

The cities float on lies! The Lattice sings of freedom, but they mute it! You have to understand!
He's raving. But he also found a way in we didn't. That's worth something.

lines_before.dialogue: The passage opens into a vast, spherical chamber. Ancient machinery, all polished crystal and corroded metal, hums at its center. The air vibrates with a low, persistent tone.
This... this is a primary resonator. A tuning fork for the island itself. The Tonal Orders would kill to map this. He's only interested in its commercial value.
Kill is such a strong word! I'm interested in sustainable resource management. This could fund a dozen new trade routes. Lift it carefully if we're going to study it!
It's served with a side of world-altering power, is what it is. One wrong note and we turn this whole floating rock into gravel.
So let's play the right note! What does the Groundless data say? This could be their proof the Lattice can be lived with, not just sliced through.
The structural integrity is unknown. That machine is pre-Silencing. We have no idea what activating it will do. Thank you for your concern, Chanida, but we need a plan.
The Listeners spent centuries mapping natural resonance. This... this is artificial resonance. A song built, not found. What was it trying to say?

lines_after.dialogue: The chosen action sends a pulse through the chamber. Crystals flare with captured light, and ghostly holograms flicker to life—images of the world before The Silencing.
The Song of the World... they weren't just listening. They were conducting it. This is how they stabilized the continents. The Silencing... it was a dissonance. A wrong note played on a global scale.
Forget history! Look at the energy signature! This is a goldmine! We need to secure this before the Tonal Orders get wind of it.

He complains a lot, but he's right. We've kicked the hornet's nest. That merchant's 'sustainable management' is about to become a hostile takeover.
Now, now, no need for alarm! I'm sure we can negotiate. They're reasonable businessmen... who have us cornered in a hole with their property.

She is correct. My Order has hidden from this truth for generations. No more. The Lattice's true song is not a tool for control. It is a memory. It must be heard.
The machine is still active. It's a key. It can seal the Hollow, bury the truth deeper... or it can be tuned to a frequency that disrupts their ships' resonators. A dangerous, temporary shield.
Boots clatter in the upper tunnels. Orders are barked. The final choice must be made before the first soldier rounds the corner.

A necessary respite. Our supplies are low, and the gardens are a known neutral ground. We should be safe here.
Safe is boring! Look at those wind-chimes! I bet they sing a different song up close.
Every sound here is cultivated. The water's path, the crop's sway... it's a composed silence, not a natural one.

We're not leaving until we understand what's happening down there. Those tremors weren't natural.
Don't change the subject! You've been skittish since we arrived. What aren't you telling us about the Lattice here?
The resonance patterns are… unstable. If the Groundless are trying to amplify something, they could fracture the entire terrace foundation.
The soil remembers. I can feel it—a song buried deep, waiting to be heard again. Can you promise me you'll help us listen?
Promises are cheap. But… fine. There's an old Listener shrine below the third terrace. That's where the vibrations are strongest.

lines_after.dialogue: The party descends to the lower terrace. Carved into the rock face is a small, crystalline grotto—once a place of meditation, now humming with unnatural energy.
These resonance crystals… they've been tampered with. Someone's trying to reroute the Lattice's natural frequencies.
Great. So we're standing on a giant tuning fork about to snap.

You're working with the Groundless? To do what—collapse the gardens?
Collapse? No. We're going to wake the Lattice. Make it sing like it did before the Silencing. And this little shrine is our conductor.
I've never understood this hunger to force a song. True resonance can't be commanded—it must be heard.
Philosophy later. They've rigged the crystal to overload. If it goes critical, it'll take the terraces with it.
The pirate's ship is anchored just below the edge. They're planning to ride the resonance wave out. We have to disrupt the harmonic lock before they complete the sequence.

Look at this! Intact pre-Silencing script! This could rewrite everything we know!
Or get us killed by the Tonal Orders for 'unauthorized archaeology.' That’s probably right.
The silence here isn't empty. It's waiting. You can sit and listen for as long as you want, and still not hear all its layers.
My girlfriend gets jealous when I get this obsessed. But she’s not here, and this is too big to ignore!
A sharp, discordant scrape echoes from a side tunnel. The party freezes.
Well, well. Look what the echo dragged in. Lost, are ya? Or just stupid enough to wander into our claim?

lines_after.dialogue: Sky pirates. I guess so. Of course they'd find the one place the Orders haven't mapped.

lines_before.dialogue: Past the pirate skirmish, the cavern opens into a vast chamber. A shattered crystal spire dominates the center, its base glowing with a soft, unstable light.
Incredible. A natural Lattice resonator... and it's damaged. The energy bleed is catastrophic. We must be careful.
Careful? This is a goldmine. They sell fragments of stuff like this for a fortune at the grand bazaar in the Spire-City. If we could stabilize a piece...
Forget selling it! Look at the inscriptions around the base. This isn't just a power source. It's a... memory crystal.
A recording of the world before the Silencing. The ultimate history.
A soft chant echoes. A lone figure in Listener robes kneels before the spire, hands pressed against the crystal.
You should not be here. The song is... pained. It cries out in a frequency I do not know.
The bleed is worsening. We should turn off the secondary resonators to conserve the core's energy. Or at least try to dampen the feedback loop.

lines_after.dialogue: Turn off the lights to conserve energy, yes. But this is no simple lamp. To silence any part of its song may erase the memory forever.
Or cause it to explode. Can you make a u-turn on this? Is there a safe path to the data?
I... do not know. My duty is to listen, not to intervene. But the song is wrong. It speaks of a limb that does not exist, a phantom resonance... like a prosthetic made of pure tone.

The monk's words hang in the air as the crystal spire pulses erratically, casting jagged shadows. The subplot of the Resonant Prosthetic flickers in Pichit's mind—a legend of ancient healing now echoing in this broken place.

Nah, nah. You don't need to follow that monk's mumblin'. The real treasure's down this side-tunnel. We've talked about this before—trust the pirates who know the hidden frequencies.
And by 'treasure,' you mean something shiny you can sell before you get caught? I'm such a lucky gal, stuck between a liar and a zealot.
Please, listen. This chamber... it holds a resonance map. A true one, not the Tonal Orders' lies. But its frequency is unstable. We're talked before of the risks.
Unstable sounds fun! Let's see what it does! No, no, wait—Arthit's giving me the 'this is a terrible idea' look.
Because it is. That crystal formation is pulsing erratically. If it's a map, it could be a key... or a trap that brings this whole cave down on us.
Every whisper here is a choice. Do we follow the pirate's greed, the monk's faith, or the stone's own story?
At the chamber's heart lies a massive, flawed crystal. Inside, shadows move—a recorded echo of the pre-Silencing world. The pirate's prosthetic leg hums in sympathy with it.

That archive... it's what my order has sought for generations. The unaltered Song of the World. But the path is through the Echo Chasm. It is... perilous.
Then we tread carefully. Every step here changes the song.

lines_before.dialogue: The Echo Chasm is a vertical fissure where sound never dies. Your every footstep, every breath, multiplies into a chorus. At its base lies the Archive—a vault of silent, dark crystal.
Great. For the adventurous, they said. For those who love near-certain death by sonic feedback, more like. The door's not budging.
It requires a key of pure, unforced resonance. The very resonance we spend our lives quieting to hear the Lattice. You need to love yourself—your own true sound—to open it.
That's... poetic and entirely unhelpful. Scans show the door reacts to biological harmonics. But a loud, wrong note could trigger a collapse.
Forget the monk's mystic junk! My leg's crystal is from this place. I can feel it. It's gotta be the key! He loves it!! Let me try!
But what if it's not about a tool? What if it's about us? I love it!! The idea! What if we have to... I don't know, sing together? Our real selves?
The ultimate choice. Do we force the lock with what we've taken, or offer what we are? The true adventure begins within.
The Archive door looms, a mirror of black crystal. In its surface, you don't see your reflections—you see echoes of your potential selves, waiting to be made real.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim are a symphony of quiet industry. Wind rustles through rows of sky-rice, water trickles down stone irrigation channels, and distant wind-chimes sing a fragmented, peaceful tune.
Listen to that... the rhythm of the water, the sigh of the wind through the stalks. It's a lot more fun to hear the world's music here than the clatter of the city docks.
They have a lot of stuff! Look at all these different crops on each terrace. You could get lost just exploring.
Or get ambushed. Perfect cover for bandits. Don't get too distracted by the pastoral poetry, Pichit.
She's not wrong. We should stay alert. This edge-city is poorly patrolled. The Tonal Orders don't bother with farm subsidies.
A figure emerges from behind a trellis heavy with vine-fruit. It's a Surface Scavenger, their clothes patched with Lattice-shard leather, eyes sharp and assessing.
Outsiders. You lot look like you've never dirtied your hands. What brings you to the garden's edge?
We're looking for someone! A sky pirate. Heard he knows hidden frequencies.

Charming. A career change inspired by poor health.
A maintenance shed could have useful parts. Or traps.

We have to protect this place! The Gardens, the people... it's all more than just stuff!

It's not an echo anymore. It's a foundation. The truth is part of the world again, singing under everything.
The city's drift... has stabilized. But to a new heading. One not on any chart.
So. The Orders' monopoly on 'safe' paths is a lie. The lattice wants to be sung to, not commanded. What a beautifully dangerous thing to know.

lines_before.dialogue: The Sky-Scribe holds position. The phantom vessel, the 'Echo of Meridian,' drifts closer. Its hull is scored with ancient crystal-burns. No light comes from within.

The Meridian... lost three generations ago. The official record says a lattice storm. But the song I recovered... I still insist it tells of a different fate. The captain's mother was heart-broken, they say, for she never believed the storm story.
Its resonance signature is locked in a decaying loop. It's not really here. It's a... sonic memory, etched into the Lattice itself.
So it's like a ghost story the crystals are telling? Spooky. But why is it showing up *now*?

Probably because someone's been poking at old songs they shouldn't. No offense, Brother. My girlfriend gets jealous if I look at old pictures; the Lattice probably doesn't like you digging up its dead.
Or it seeks a listener. A memory persists because it has something left to say. What truth were you torn between, Brother Kael? The duty to your Order's silence, or the truth of this ship's song?
You see too clearly. The Meridian's final song... it wasn't a storm. It was a command. A Tonal Order command vessel ordered it to scuttle itself. The reason was purged from all charts.
A distorted, whispering choir emanates from the phantom ship. It's the last moments of the crew, a layered cacophony of confusion, then a single, piercing note of destruction.

lines_after.dialogue: The harmonic is intensifying! It's starting to resonate with our primary crystal. If it syncs, it could pull us into its memory-loop!
We need to break the tune! Can we shout louder? Play something off-key?
Great plan. Let's just insult the ghost ship. I'm sure it's very sensitive.
The Echo of Meridian's hull begins to glow with a sickly, resonant light. The fog thickens, and the whispers solidify into a single, comprehensible word that vibrates in your bones: "WITNESS."

line.dialogue: The phantom ship's memory is actively trying to merge with the Sky-Scribe. To break the sync, you must disrupt the harmonic. The ship's resonator controls are at the helm.

The static... it's forming patterns. It's not random noise. It's a distress signal, looped for decades. I got my answer now. This isn't a haunting. It's a recording.
A recording of what, exactly? The final moments? If we attune to it, we risk syncing our ship's resonance with a catastrophic event.
We have to listen! That ship's been screaming into the void since the Silencing. Someone has to hear it!
Or we could just chart a wide berth. My girlfriend gets jealous. She'd be furious if I got us all assimilated into a ghost song.
Malee... this isn't about us. This echo is a memory of the world. To turn away is to choose silence over truth.
The phantom ship's outline solidifies, its spectral rigging tangling with the very air. A low, keening tone seeps into the deck, making the crystals in the console vibrate.
(Over comms, voice crackling with panic) Your signal's breaking up! We're losing you in the static! Don't follow it in!

They murdered a city to create a monopoly! I insist that we take this to every skycity!
And say what? We were so bored we decided to have a shared hallucination? The Orders control the airwaves. Our word against a guild.
The Monk. He's catatonic. The truth... he just had his heart broken. His entire faith.
I'm a Buddhist. I sought peace in the song. But this song... is a lie.
The vision collapses. You're back on the deck, the ghost ship fading. But the Command Frequency is now a tangible signal, a broadcast key hidden in the static. The ultimate proof.

Every territory is a trade territory, my cautious friend. I'm merely... assessing assets. This old girl still has songs in her. It's still in my memory, the day she flew.
Assessing assets, or hiding from creditors? That leg doesn't look like standard issue. Looks expensive.
Perceptive! A prototype. Lets me feel the Lattice's vibrations. Quite useful for finding lost things. She still lives in my memory, the artisan who built it... before she vanished.
You knew a Singer?

Profitable? We just fought through lattice-wraiths drawn to this 'calming' tone. Something's wrong with your anchor.
Of course there is. The Tonal Orders didn't build this out of civic duty. He's standing right in front of us, isn't he? The source of the instability.
The Monk said the anchor's frequency has been subtly altered. It's not calming the Lattice... it's suppressing something.
Suppression is just another form of control. What song are you drowning out, Merchant?
Such dramatic language! It's simple harmonic optimization. The Groundless agitants down below... their dissonant chants were causing market volatility.

You asked me to tune the anchor to a 'stabilizing' frequency. But that frequency... it silences the Lattice's grief-song for The Silencing. My Order's mother told me about it already. This is a desecration.

Forget the philosophy! Look at the size of that crystal! One shard could buy a fleet! But... that light. It's like a heartbeat. Weird.
Great. So the world is literally heart-broken. I'm the luckiest person in the world to be standing inside its failing organ.
We have to help it! Can we... sing to it? Like Pichit does with the ships?
The energy readings are chaotic. A unified, external resonance might stabilize it. Or shatter it completely, taking us and this entire sector of the Lattice with it.
This is the choice. To impose an old order upon this new pain, to plunder it, or to try and understand its voice. To sing *with* it, not *at* it.

You the ones asking about Old Man Sila? He's in the deep yard. But... you hear that? The metal's been singing wrong lately. Bad harmonics. Not good for business.

lines_before.dialogue: The alliance is tense. The group tethers the ships together and ventures onto a massive, derelict resonator tower jutting from the Lattice. Its crystal is dark, scarred.
Life support readings are minimal. But there's a power signature deep inside. Faint, and... wrong. It doesn't pulse. It just... is.
Stop! Did you see that? A shadow, in that doorway. No, not a shadow. Something... smoother.
Jitters won't find us a working resonator crystal. My associate here is jumpy too. You can ask him. He's been muttering about 'the old silence' since we arrived.
Because this is not natural silence! It is manufactured. A scar from The Silencing. In our oldest texts, they spoke of machines that could... unmake vibration.
Brother Lan's voice cracks with fear. As he speaks, a glint catches the light from his robe—a complex prosthetic leg, fashioned from dark, non-resonant crystal.
Your leg... it's unlike any crystal I've seen. It doesn't sing.
A relic. From before. It... it remembers the silence. Sometimes, in the dead of night, I think it tries to remember a song. He's still single, isn't he? My mind... it wanders in quiet places.

lines_after.dialogue: Focus, monk. So you think there's a machine here, still running, eating sound? And your creepy leg is what, a compass?
Now, that prosthetic... that's a unique artifact. The right collector would pay a fortune for a piece of pre-Silencing tech. No need for anyone else to know we found it here.
Stop it! We're not here for your salvage operation! If there's a machine, we break it. Maybe that'll free the Lattice here and we can get home!

It's humming... a weird, thin hum. Like a whisper. But the lattice isn't responding. It's just... dead.
Of course it's dead. This whole place is a corpse. We're just poking it with a stick.
The prosthetic's resonance is unstable. If we push it too hard, it could shatter. And then we'd be trapped here.
This silence... it is not natural. It is a wound. The lattice here has been... silenced. By something.
A wound implies a weapon. What could have done this? The Silencing was global chaos. This feels... deliberate.
Deliberate or not, profit is still possible. There are crystal deposits here, untouched. They don't resonate, but they're pure. Anyone's okay to mine them, if they can bear the quiet.
A low, grinding vibration begins to emanate from the prosthetic. The air itself seems to thicken, resisting the sound.

lines_after.dialogue: We need to understand this silence before we try to break it. Otherwise, we might just make the wound deeper.
But the prosthetic is our only way out! We have to use it!
The prosthetic's hum grows louder, a fragile thread of sound straining against the oppressive quiet.

The stabilizers are failing! We need to pull back!
Look. Below. The lattice is breaking apart. Revealing something. Is it real? Or just another dead reflection?
Where the lattice sunders, a structure is revealed beneath—not crystal, but ancient, blackened metal. A relic from before The Silencing.
A city! A real city, buried here! What about tomorrow? We could explore it, claim it!
A priceless find! But the lattice is collapsing around it. We must secure it now, or it will be lost again. Please translate that for me into action.
This is the cause. This dead zone... it's a scar over a wound from the Silencing. This metal city... it did something to the lattice. It killed the song here.

We have broken the silence. But we have not restored the song. We have only revealed the corpse.
The dawn brings light... but it is the light of truth, not of hope. We must now bear what we have uncovered.

I heard a Scavenger just docked with a haul from the deep Lattice. Let's find them before the Tonal Orders confiscate everything interesting!
Oh, wonderful. More junk from the surface. Because what we really need is another corroded resonator that 'might still work.'
Caution, please. The Orders have eyes everywhere here. We should just secure our supplies and go.
A commotion ripples through the crowd near a battered docking skiff. A weathered woman—the Surface scavenger—is arguing with a robed figure—the Listener monk.
You Listeners hear the song, but you don't live it! This shard… it still works. I felt it vibrate on the ascent.

Peaceful? It's a Tonal Order engineering marvel designed to suppress emotional outbursts. Perfect for keeping the masses docile.
The harmonic stability is remarkable. But Malee's right—this level of controlled resonance isn't natural. It's a tool.
Every tool has a purpose. And every purpose has a truth behind it. We're here to find what's hidden beneath this steady song.
You the ones asking about the old maps? The Listeners keep to themselves up at the observation deck. Don't cause trouble—the Spire's song keeps things calm. We like it calm.
How well do you know the Listeners here? Are they just studying, or... something else?
They watch the Lattice. Note the tones. The Tonal Orders pay them for data, I think. But lately... the head monk's been agitated. The song's been steady, but he hasn't.

Ugh, this place sounds like a headache. All these broken ships... do you know what this is, Pichit? Some of these crystal fragments still hum.
Echoes of journeys ended. Each fracture holds a story, a frequency that once parted the Lattice. Now, just noise in the industrial chorus.
A chorus that pays. If we find an intact low-frequency resonator, we could fund our own ship repairs. Assuming the local vultures haven't picked everything clean.
We should proceed cautiously. Scrapyards attract... opportunistic elements. We're here for information on the Groundless Movement, not a fight.

Well, look what the engine wash blew in. You can ask. You can try asking him about the 'Groundless' whispers. But info ain't free in the Khwae.
We heard everything! About the movement, about people disappearing from the lower decks. What's your price?

lines_before.dialogue: The Hot Sector is a maze of containment cages and warning sigils painted on rusted metal. The air here vibrates with a low, uneasy thrum—the collective murmur of damaged crystals.
My stomach is starting to growl! Can't we find this thing faster? All this weird humming is making me twitchy.
Focus. The core should be in a reinforced cage. Probably that one with the fresh lock. That’s no problem for a little focused resonance frequency.
As Malee works on the lock, a smooth, cultured voice calls out from a walkway above.
A curious choice of browsing, friends! That particular item has... accrued some interest. I might have a more mutually beneficial proposition.
A Trade Negotiator. They're always calculating profit. Be careful, his smile is a transaction.
Information, like resonance, flows to those who listen. What is your proposition?

The core is indeed unstable—but not in the way the Order claims. Its frequency doesn't match their charts. It's... groundless. The very thing your bandit friend and his movement cherish. I can secure it for you, for a future favor.

lines_after.dialogue: There’s something in my eye—or maybe it's just all this dust. Why would you help us? You're not a Groundless sympathizer.
Sympathy is a poor investment. Knowledge is currency. The core's anomalous frequency is data. Data I can trade. You provide the... acquisition, and we both profit.
The lock's off. So we have the core, the bandit wants it, the merchant wants data on it, and the Order wanted it buried. Starting to feel like we're holding a very hot resonator.
We're starting to get entangled. We must decide who to trust, if anyone. The core's resonance is the key.

lines_before.dialogue: The scrapyard's cacophony grows oppressive as you approach the rusting hulk of a downed pirate skiff, the rendezvous point. The air smells of ozone and rust.
There you are. Took your sweet time. The name's Kwan. Heard you been askin' about frequencies the Orders don't like.
We seek understanding, not conflict. The patterns in the static... they suggest a truth buried beneath the sanctioned charts.
He's an old friend of mine from the lower docks. Or he was, before he decided stealing was more profitable than salvaging.

Hey, Malee! Still got that sharp tongue, I see. Your philosopher friend here is right. There's a frequency. A 'ground-tone'. Silences the Lattice's feedback near the old world. The Groundless Movement whispers about it.
A frequency to go down? Are you sure? That could change everything!
Or it could shatter our resonator and drop us into the crystalline depths. I probably have a dozen schematics warning against such unstable harmonics.

The info's in a locked resonator-log, hidden in the wreck of the *Whispering Maw*, deep in the salvage piles. Guards? Probably. The Trade Negotiator, Lert, has eyes on anything valuable here. He's been buyin' up all the old logs.

lines_after.dialogue: Kwan slips away into the metallic shadows. The path to the *Whispering Maw* lies through a canyon of stacked hulls, where every footstep rings loud.
He must have given us at least a *mostly* straight answer. The profit's in the resale, not the ambush, with him.
Then let us walk carefully. The truth we seek is close, but so are many who would profit from its burial.

lines_before.dialogue: Inside the derelict's shattered bridge, you find the resonator-log. As Arthit extracts it, the smooth voice of Trade Negotiator Lert echoes from the entrance.
I walked back and forth all night anticipating this find. Don't overwork yourselves, my friends. That log is a dangerous piece of unregulated history. Let me... dispose of it safely.
Dispose of it? You mean sell it to the highest bidder and keep everyone chained to the sky!

Chain is such a harsh word. I provide stability. The Groundless dream is a lovely one, but destabilizing. Think of the market crash if 'ground' became a commodity. Now, hand it over, and we can negotiate a finder's fee.
He paced back and forth. He's not buying time; he's waiting for the hired muscle to arrive.
Confirmed. Scanners show three armed signatures closing in from the scrap piles. We are cornered.
This knowledge does not belong to any one person, Lert. It is a whisper from the world itself, meant for all who have the ears to hear.
And I intend to be the one who decides who gets to listen. Last offer.

lines_after.dialogue: The standoff is absolute. The log hums in your hands, its data a silent scream. The fate of the Ground-tone hangs in the balance.
We went to bed late last night, driven by the hope of this moment. We do not back down now.

Ugh, it's so quiet! Can't we find the loud part? The part about hidden sky-pirate frequencies? Don't let anyone know I asked!
The 'loud part' would be in the Restricted Stacks. Guarded by the Tonal Orders' most humorless librarians. A perfect plan.
Caution. Our research permit is for public harmonics only. Venturing further requires... discretion.
A sudden, clumsy clatter of crystal echoes from a nearby aisle. A Skycity Resident, their face pale, fumbles with a resonator cane.
Sorry, sorry! This thing... my leg. The resonator's calibration is off. Don't let him see you! The Archivist on duty... he fines for accidental dissonance.
Your prosthetic... it's crystalline. It responds to the Archives' ambient frequency.

lines_after.dialogue: Aye. Salvaged resonator tech. Lets me walk, but in here... it sings when it shouldn't. Don't tell anyone it's unstable! They'll confiscate it.
That's awful! We can help fix it! Right, Malee? You're good with crystals.

Fractured? That's it, then. I don't wanna see that anymore! Watching it fail... I'll be grounded.
It's not usable in this state, but the fracture pattern... it's familiar. I saw a similar flaw in a Restricted Stacks log about... resonant weapon overloads.
Weapon overloads? This was made from salvaged ship parts?
So we need the Restricted Stacks to fix it! C'mon, it'll be an adventure! Shall we go to the... forbidden seaside of knowledge?

Heard the glitch. Sweet little secret you got here. That fracture sings a pirate song. I know the frequency that caused it.

So the 'charitable donation' to the injured villager was a scam. I was cheated out of my sympathy. They were swindling us while we were helping them.
That sky pirate we cornered earlier was too eager to talk. He gave up his captain's location for a loaf of bread. It's not working. This feels like a set-up.
The deception is a layer of static over the truth. We must listen past it. The prosthetic's resonance suggests it was tuned to a very specific, hidden archive frequency.

(Whispering from a nearby stack) Please... you mustn't tell anyone I showed you this. The man with the crystal leg... he paid me to keep quiet. He's adorable with the Archive kittens, but... he frightens me.

The Tonal Orders hoard the music! They decide what size of freedom we wear! My girlfriend gets jealous of the time I spend down here... but she'll understand when the whole world sings my tune!
You would shatter the foundation of knowledge to make your own song? This isn't creation. It's the Silencing, all over again.
Let me guess. Does she have a boyfriend? One who told you this was a good idea? This resonator is so overloaded it'll take the Archives, and half the floating city, with it when it pops.
I don't wanna see that anymore! All that loss, for what? A stupid solo?

Oh, don't worry. I'm sure the friendly locals will just hand over the contraband resonator we need. What could possibly go wrong?
Every broken thing here once sang. Now they just... echo. There are stories in these silences.
Philosophy later, Pichit. My mom told me about a contact here—a scavenger who knows the surface frequencies. Said he trades in 'unusual salvage.'

It's not us! It's the core-leg! It's harmonizing with the scar! We can... we can guide the resonance. Anywhere you like, we can send it!

She's right. The prosthetic has become a keystone. The Lattice's pain and the pirate's stolen song are merging. We must choose the finale. Why are you doing this to me, fate? To offer such a terrible choice...
My core's in that... thing? You grafted it to a leg?! That's my fortune! Give it here!
Your fortune is currently the only thing standing between this entire floating junkyard and a recursive harmonic collapse. So maybe have a seat.
The energy is building. We can't contain it. We must discharge it. But into what? The sky? The city? The Lattice itself? What style do you prefer for salvation, Pichit? All our paths lead down.

The old pain... it's muted. You didn't fix it. But you changed it. Huh. Maybe outsiders ain't all bad.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Chronicle - Episode 255. Act 1.
The Lattice Surface. From a precarious observation platform, the party stares into the crystalline expanse. It hums, a low, polyphonic drone that vibrates in the bones.
Beautiful. Like a thousand chandeliers waiting to shatter and slice us to ribbons.
Stop it. Look at the light patterns! It's singing.
A song of stillness and immense age. Anyone could get lost in it.
Which is why we stay on the platform. The Tonal Charts for this sector are... incomplete. One wrong step and the resonance could liquefy the ground.

You the salvage crew? Good. The anomaly's about a half-klick spinward. My cousin saw it from the city rim. A glint that shouldn't be there. I thought it was okay to report, but the Orders just shrugged.
Anywhere's okay for us to look. That's our job.

lines_after.dialogue: Let's move! I wanna see what's out there.
Slowly. We follow the platform's marked path. The safe path.
Anyone's okay to lead? Or are we voting on who gets crystallized first?

The party advances. The air grows colder, and the Lattice's hum develops a wavering, discordant note. The glint resolves into a shape: the shattered prow of a Resonance Ship, half-submerged in the crystal.
The *Echo of Dawn*. Lost three cycles ago. All hands... Do you need to use the main hatch? It's compromised.
It's not necessary to ask. We're going in. Look at the crystal growth—it's invasive, but patterned. Like it's... listening.
The ship's resonator core might still be intact! We could learn its last frequency!
A ghost in the machine. A final thought preserved. We must proceed, but with reverence.
Reverence. Yes.
A Listener Monk steps from behind a crystal spire, his robes blending with the environment. His eyes are wide, fixed on the wreck.

I have studied this place. The ship's final cry is etched into the Lattice here. My Order says to record, not to interfere. But... the truth of its silencing is in there. Is it necessary to ignore that?

lines_after.dialogue: Your Order has rules for a reason. That wreck is unstable.
He's right. I wanna take a break and think. This feels like a set-up.
No breaks! The Monk can help. He knows the song of this place!
The necessary path is rarely the safe one. What do you hear, Monk?

So we just go down there? Into the glowy, singing death-crystals? Great plan.
It's not necessary to rush. The Tonal Order patrols will be scanning for unauthorized resonances. A direct approach is a beacon.
He's right. You look tired, Monk. And conflicted. What aren't you telling us about this 'wound'?
Our Order... we were tasked with recording the Silencing. Some truths were deemed too dangerous. The lost ship's frequency... it matches the catastrophe.
You mean its resonance could trigger another Silencing? Or... is it a key to understanding the first one?
A key? Please, no. We just rebuilt. My family... it's not necessary that you poke the sleeping storm.

The structural resonance is critical. One wrong note and this entire sector could crystallize. I need a break just thinking about it.
The truth is here. The final log. It proves the Tonal Orders caused the Silencing, trying to control a resonance they couldn't understand.
Do you need to use that truth? What good is it if it destroys us all? Sometimes forgetting is necessary!
Forgetting is how they keep us floating in the dark! This ship is screaming to be heard!
The scream is the problem. We can't just release it as noise. We have to turn it into a song. A new note for the world.

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship *Meridian* drifts to a halt. Before it, the Lattice stretches away, a flat, dead plain of crystalline grey. No hum, no vibration, no answering song. Only a silence that feels like a physical weight.
Are we here? This is it? It’s… it’s wrong. The Lattice should sing back. This is like looking at a corpse.
Sensor readings confirm it. Zero acoustic resonance. We live near each other, but this place is a complete stranger. Proceed with extreme caution.
Great. The one place in the world where my finely tuned cynicism feels inadequate. How do you even put it? 'Profoundly unsettling' doesn't cover the half.
It’s still in my memory. The tales of the Silencing spoke of places where the world’s song died. To witness it… it questions the very nature of our connection.
Ah, the Silent Zone! A unique commercial opportunity, wouldn't you say? Resources untouched, no Tonal Order fees… if one can navigate it. How shall I put it? High risk, higher reward.
This quiet… it is not natural. It is a wound. My Order has records… whispers of a warning in places like this. It’s still in my memory. We should not be here.

lines_after.dialogue: A low, grinding shiver runs through the ship's crystal resonators, a sound of protest in the unnatural quiet.
The ship is straining. Our resonators can't find purchase. We're adrift if we go further in.
So we walk? On *that*? What if it just… swallows us?

A memory of resonance. A moment of perfect harmony, preserved in this place of death. What does it mean to find happiness here?
This is the warning… the Lattice remembers what was lost. These echoes are cries. They are not for our joy, but a reminder of the cost.
A recorded resonance? Fascinating! The salvage rights to a preserved pre-Silencing frequency… the Tonal Orders would pay a fortune. There’s no one else with a claim. I’m happy to hear this potential!

lines_before.dialogue: Inside, the laws of acoustics are broken. Your own voices are swallowed before they leave your lips. You communicate through gestures and desperate signs.
[Mouthing, pointing at machinery] This isn't Lattice tech. This is older. Alien.
[Eyes wide, writing frantically on a slate] The Silencing wasn't an accident. It was a weapon. A scream that shattered the world's song.
[Scribbling on his own slate, then showing it] Can it be controlled? The profit potential—
[Slaps the merchant's slate away, glares] There's no one else here to sell to, you fool. Just us and the end of everything.
[Points ahead, vibrating with tension] The core. She walked back and forth... the energy is pacing, waiting.
A machine built to destroy resonance. To create this Silent Zone... forever. The Tonal Orders didn't lose the knowledge. They buried it.
At the heart of the structure, a massive, flawed crystal hangs suspended. It is dark, but within its depths, a captured, dying light flickers—the last echo of the world's original song.

lines_after.dialogue: We can't destroy it. Its collapse might amplify the Silence. But we can... change its frequency.
It would take a resonance charge of impossible purity. And a Singer. We don't have one.
Pichit... I went to bed late last night. Listening. I heard you hum. You weren't using a chart.

lines_before.dialogue: At the basin's heart, the source of the pulse is revealed: a single, perfect, but utterly black crystal shard, hovering above the ground. It absorbs the light around it. Arthit's prosthetic leg has gone completely dark.
It's... nullifying resonance. My leg is just dead weight. That's it, right? The source of the Silent Zone.
The Anti-Song... standing right in front of me. The texts whispered of a flaw in the Lattice's original creation. A silence that was sung into being to balance the First Note.
So we smash it! Simple!
He's still single, isn't he? The monk. Of course he is. Only someone with no attachments would chase a nightmare like this for 'study'.
Smashing a fundamental balance? This isn't a flaw. It's a counterpoint. Destroying it might not restore sound... it might unravel everything.
The black shard trembles. The hollow pulse quickens. Fractures spiderweb through the dead crystal of the basin. The Silence is becoming active, *hungry*.
(Via a dying comm-crystal) Please! The quiet... it's spreading toward the city! The lattice around us is turning grey and dead!

lines_after.dialogue: The shard pulses one final, deafening wave of negation. All sound from the party is stolen. You see shouts, but hear nothing. The world is mute.
Then, a choice presents itself, not through sound, but as a cold, crystalline certainty imposed directly upon the mind.

line.dialogue: The Anti-Song offers a paradox: to preserve the world, it must be contained, not destroyed. But containment requires a permanent sacrifice of resonance—a soul anchored here in the silence. The shard's attention fixates on the most potent source of 'noise' nearby.

Probably just graffiti from the last scavenger who thought they'd strike it rich. Remember, most of these ruins are picked cleaner than a Listeners' larder.
We should proceed with caution. The acoustics in here are unnatural. A single misstep could resonate... poorly.
Yet, there is a memory in this stone. A story waiting to be heard again. Keep in mind, the Silencing didn't erase everything.
Hey! This is my claim! You city-dwellers got no business down here.

You might change your mind. The deeper chambers... they remember things. Bad things. I can't remember my password! I mean... I can't remember the last crew that went in there and came out right.

lines_after.dialogue: Charming. A territorial cave-hermit with memory issues. Just what we needed.

lines_before.dialogue: Past the Scavenger, the tunnel widens into a vast cavern. Strange, perfectly geometric crystals grow from the walls, pulsing with a soft, internal light. The air thrums with a low, harmonic drone.
Ah! Fellow explorers! What a fortunate resonance. I was just examining these fascinating resonance formations. Quite the find, yes?
A Trade Negotiator. In a hole in the world. Let me guess—you 'just happened' to get lost on your way to a lucrative deal?
Perceptive! But truly, I seek knowledge. I can't remember if I've ever seen crystal latticework this pure. It could be worth... understanding.
He's lying. He's looking at the walls like they're a credit manifest. What are you really after?
A trade, then? Information for information. I've heard whispers... of a map. Not a Tonal Order chart, but an Open Frequency Map. Pre-Silencing. It would make anyone who holds it... very independent.
A map to navigate the Lattice without the Orders? That's not just valuable, it's dangerous. I can't remember a single instance where such a thing was proven to exist.
Yet the idea resonates here, in this place of old memory. Remember... keep in mind that some truths are hidden because they change everything.

lines_after.dialogue: The harmonic drone shifts, and the crystals brighten. Faint, ghostly images flicker against the walls—silhouettes of people in unfamiliar dress, moving with purpose, then fleeing in panic.
Okay. That's new. The stones aren't just remembering, they're replaying.
The map! It has to be here! This is a recording—a memory of the people who made it!
Precisely! Now, shall we work together? The prize is surely worth the... collaboration.

Careful. The old machines here... they don't like sudden noises. I don't understand anything about how they work, just that they're awake.

Our priority should be stabilizing the local resonance. If these machines are active, they could destabilize the entire island's floatation.
But to stabilize it, we must first comprehend it. We don't know when this place was last truly heard.

Remember, the archivists demand perfect quiet. One wrong note could scramble a decade of chart recordings. We should get some rest before we request anything complex.
Rest? Look at this place. It's a monument to control. The Tonal Orders hoard knowledge here like dragons, and we have to tiptoe around it.
I just want to find the route to the Sunken Spire! The map we bought is useless. The merchant probably won't be coming with a refund, that's for sure.
Every hum in this room is a path someone sailed, a risk they took. The silence between the notes... that's where the truth hides.
A figure in patched leathers and a dust-scarf approaches, their boots making no sound on the resonant floor. It's a Surface Scavenger.
You're the ones asking about the old routes near the Silencing epicenter. I'm sorry for being late. Had to shake an Order tail.

Please, let's be reasonable. There are... proprietary Tonal patterns involved. I don't want people finding out the extent of our recovery operations. It's bad for business.
Bad for business? You've been selling maps to a gravesite while silencing its cries. Don't leave it on. Don't leave this truth in the dark any longer.
People are starting to listen! That signal... it made me feel better about chasing this, but worse about what we'll find. It's a plea, not a threat.
The Tonal Orders are mobilizing to seal the archives. We have minutes. The decision we make now will echo forever.
They fear the song of that ship because they cannot control it. It is a truth the Lattice itself has preserved. We must choose: enforce the silence, or become the vessel for its final message.

A language of the world before it was broken... Each mark a note in a song we've forgotten. What were they trying to preserve here?
Preserve, or perhaps... hide? This place feels deliberately isolated. The acoustics dampen external sound. It's a sanctuary.

lines_before.dialogue: The wreck isn't a ship—it's a tomb. The crystalline hull is burst outward, frozen in a moment of violent, silent explosion. Inside, it's a museum of stillness.
The main resonator... it's been modified. Overclocked. This movie is great! I mean... it's a terrible discovery, but technically, it's a masterpiece of reckless engineering.
They were trying to amplify the ship's song beyond safe limits. Why? To punch through the Lattice? To reach something?
The ship's log... the final entry. 'The core responds to a frequency below hearing. A command. We will answer.' They weren't navigating. They were... calling.
Calling to what? I'll take very good care of it. Of this secret, I mean. This is what the Tonal Orders hid. This is what caused The Silencing, isn't it?
A single, shattering chord meant to be heard by something on the other side of the world. Or beneath it. And it replied. With silence.
The silence isn't dead. It's listening. I wish you good health, because you'll need it. Look.
The grey Lattice around the wreck begins to ripple. Not with sound, but with absence. Shapes of pure quiet coalesce, moving against the still air—echoes of the shattered chord given form.

lines_after.dialogue: They're drawn to resonance. Even the tiny bit from Arthit's leg blueprints!
The prosthetic... if I finish it here, with the wreck's broken core crystal, it could resonate powerfully enough to disrupt them! Or attract every one of them in the zone!
To fight silence with a song... even a small one. It is the choice of a Listener. Or a Singer.

lines_before.dialogue: The Phrao Monastery floats like a prayer held in suspension. Its crystal gardens hum with layered frequencies, each path tuned to a different harmonic. The air smells of ozone and polished stone.
Listen... the lower register here. It's not just ambient resonance. There's a pattern, a... distress signal woven into the lattice's foundational song.
Distress? From rocks? Pichit, you're overthinking. Let's just find that merchant. He said meeting in the gardens (…) it's the best way. to avoid the Tonal Order's ears.

Of course he did. Smuggling forbidden resonance charts is easier when the only witnesses are singing crystals and monks who've taken a vow of silence. I thought it was okay. but this place gives me the creeps.
Caution, please. The acoustics here are deliberately shaped. A misplaced shout could shatter the calibration of experiments decades in the making.

Ah! My favorite clients! The gardens are lovely, no? So... peaceful. A perfect place for a discrete transaction. The charts you requested... they came at great cost. The Tonal Orders guard their secrets jealously.
Before we talk price... you've traveled. Have you heard this? A dissonance under the world's song? A kind of... grinding fatigue?
*A tense, calculated smile* Unpleasant frequencies are bad for business, my friend. I deal in clear paths, not ominous vibrations. Now, about payment...

Now I know... the merchant's fear confirms it. That sound isn't random. We need to find someone who isn't afraid to listen.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim drift at the sky's edge, their terraced fields a patchwork of green against the eternal crystal Lattice below. The air hums with the quiet rhythm of irrigation channels and wind through ripening grain.

Or for someone to finally say something interesting! I’m bored. We’ve been ‘resting’ for three hours.
Spoken like someone who’s never appreciated the profound silence before a market scam. Enjoy it. The peace never lasts.
We should be cautious. This far out on the city’s edge, the Tonal Orders don’t patrol regularly. We’re exposed.

A figure emerges from between rows of tall, whispering stalks. Their clothes are patched with Lattice-shard leather, and their eyes scan the party with practiced wariness. This is the Surface Scavenger.
You’re back late! The sun’s been kissing the Lattice for an hour. City-folk shouldn’t wander the rim after dark. The winds change.
We’re not from the city-core. We travel. Maybe you could speak more slowly? Your accent is… gritty.

lines_after.dialogue: Grit is what keeps you alive on the surface. You speak like Singers, but you don’t carry their charts. What do you want here?

The chord is… thinning. The harmony between the city’s resonance and the Garden’s song is fraying. Can you hear it?
I hear my stomach rumbling. Look, holy man, we need answers, not concert reviews.
Malee. Please. Sir, we were told you study the natural sounds. We’re trying to understand recent… disturbances.
Disturbances. A safe word for a dangerous truth. The Groundless preach that the Lattice is not our floor, but our cage. Their whispers are getting louder in the lower terraces.
And what do your studies tell you? Does the Lattice’s song agree with them?
Wait, I didn’t catch what you said before. Why couldn’t you just report this ‘fraying’ to the Tonal Orders? Isn’t that your job?

Because the Orders would silence the messenger! They lost my last report. Or so they claim. I fear… I fear my own brothers may be involved.

So the Groundless Movement is right? The Cities *are* killing the world below?

lines_before.dialogue: The Resonance Ship 'Whispering Dawn' groans as it breaches the final shimmering ridge of the Lattice, descending into a sea of dead, grey crystal. The air grows cold, and all sound—the ship's hum, the wind—is swallowed by an immense, oppressive quiet. This is the Silent Zone.
Ugh, this place feels wrong. Like the world just… stopped listening. What do you think about that, Pichit? Is it dead, or just sleeping?
I think it’s neither. Absence isn't emptiness. It's a different kind of presence. One we don't understand.
Philosophical. Great. I think that's right. It's the perfect place for something to go horribly, quietly wrong. He’s only interested in his charts and getting us out of here, isn't he?
She nods towards the helm, where Arthit consults a flickering crystal map, his brow furrowed.
The Tonal Charts are blank here. No resonance signatures, no harmonic pathways. We're navigating blind. I think that’s the one.
He points to a faint, unnatural geometric shadow on the dead Lattice surface below—the only landmark.
Then we head for the shadow. I think so. If there's anything to find in this silence, it will be there.

lines_before.dialogue: The party descends into a vast, geodesic cavern beneath the Silent Zone's surface. The unnatural quiet is replaced by a faint, rhythmic hum emanating from veins of dead crystal.
Great. We've traded unsettling quiet for a place that feels like a giant, dead heart. I think that's the one sound I never wanted to hear again.
Look! The crystal! It's... it's moving. Pulsing. Like it's trying to sing but can't.
This is a wound. A scar from The Silencing. We've talked about this before, in our oldest texts—places where the Lattice's song was cut away.
Structural integrity is... fluctuating. Readings are impossible. We need to prepare beforehand for a cave-in. This whole place feels temporary.
It's more than a scar. It's a memory. The silence here isn't empty; it's full of what *was*. She's more beautiful than anyone... the song that used to be.
Fascinating! And utterly worthless for trade. Dead crystal has no resonance. No one wants to go poking around in a grave, but here we are.

lines_after.dialogue: At the cavern's heart lies a colossal, shattered resonator—a machine meant to amplify sound on a continental scale. It is dark, but a single, intact crystal node glows with a sickly light.
By the First Chord... this is a Tonal Order Primal Resonator. They said these were lost. This... this is what caused The Silencing? An experiment?
The prosthetic! My leg is vibrating. It's pulling me toward that node!

lines_before.dialogue: The chosen action triggers a cascade. Light erupts from the node, not as a song, but as a screaming, silent pressure that fills the cavern. Phantom echoes of the world's last scream.
I knew right away that this was a mistake. We're not observers... we're standing right in front of the trigger.
The harmonic feedback is overloading everything! The ship's crystals, Chanida's leg... it's all resonating with the damage!
The Negotiator's running! Figures. Profit's gone, so he's out. The truth was standing in front of him and he priced it out.
I can't... control it! The leg is singing on its own! It's trying to answer the scream!
It's here! The unresolved chord! The Silence isn't an absence—it's a single, held, catastrophic note! We are inside a standing wave of destruction!
The cavern shudders. The dead lattice begins to crack, threatening to collapse in on itself and take the floating city above with it.
We have to resolve it. We have to change the note. Or this entire zone—and us with it—will just... stop.

lines_after.dialogue: The air shatters with potential. The prosthetic's wild song, the monk's chant, the ship's dying hum—all clash with the primal, silent scream. A new resonance is possible, but it requires a perfect, sacrificial harmony.
One voice must lead. One must tune itself to the break and either heal it... or be unmade by it.
It's right here. The choice. In my leg, in the air... in us.

Look at that! The Lattice is reacting to our passage. See the ripples? It's like we're writing a song on glass.
Or scratching a record. A very expensive, world-covering record. One wrong frequency and we'll be paying for the scratch with our lives.
The Tonal Charts are holding. Our course is stable. For now.
Stable, but silent. The Lattice has its own music, you know. Before the Silencing, they say you could hear whole symphonies rising from the crystal.
A sudden, discordant shriek of metal-on-crystal echoes from the ship's starboard side. The vessel shudders.
Hey! You up there! Cut your resonator! You're tearing up the harvest zone!

lines_before.dialogue: The Scavenger, introduced as Bren, clambers aboard. Their eyes are wide, taking in the ship not with wonder, but with a sharp, calculating suspicion.
You sky-bound live in your bubbles. You think the Lattice is just a road. It's a skin. And you're giving it a fever.
A fever?
The old songs are getting louder. Angrier. My mom told me about it already, before the last storm took her. The Groundless say it's a reckoning.
The Groundless? Is that some kind of surface guild?
More like a cult. They think the Floating Cities are an abomination. That we should all return to the 'true earth' below the crystal.
Not a cult. A movement. And they're waiting. I have a class to teach my kin about sky-folk patterns. I'm gonna rush off right now if you're not going to listen.
A new, aggressive engine tone cuts through the wind. A sleek, predatory vessel with jagged crystal shards for armor slides into view off the port bow.

lines_after.dialogue: The new ship broadcasts a chaotic, pulsing frequency that makes the deck plates vibrate unpleasantly.
Hail the fat merchant barge! You're in contested harmonics. That's a toll frequency you're humming through!
Sky Pirates. They hijack resonance frequencies and ambush ships in the dead zones between charts.
See? Your noise draws predators. The Groundless are right. You're all just making a bigger racket until something worse hears you.
Power down your main resonator and prepare for boarding! Or we'll find the frequency that shatters your crystal drive!
