The frequency interference is overwhelming the resonator! We're losing altitude. We should wait for the rain to stop… if this static-storm ever ends.
Brilliant observation. The ship's failing, and your solution is to hope the hostile sky changes its mind. It still works as a plan to crash.
Forget waiting! Look—scavenger skiffs, closing in from the Lattice spires. And another ship on the horizon. Pirates?
(Over the comms, voice crackling with static) Surface-dwellers to drifting fools. Your song is sick. You're leaking resonance. Drawing the wrong kind of attention.
Attention from whom? The Silencing wasn't an accident… it was a command. And something down there is listening for disobedient voices.
The pirate ship, a jagged construct of salvaged metal, banks hard. Its resonator emits a predatory, shrieking frequency aimed at your ship's core.

(Over a shrill comm channel) Hah! Found you, songbirds! Hand over your crystal charts and maybe we won't shatter your hull. You don't need to be Number 1 in the sky to survive… just smarter than the next target.

lines_before.dialogue: The consequences of your maneuver unfold. The pirate ship veers, its predatory shriek warping. The scavenger skiffs scatter. But from the Lattice itself, a deep, resonant HUM begins, shaking the very air.
(Voice urgent, cutting through the hum) It's awake! The old pulse beneath the Spire of Whispers! You've stirred it! Don't let it see you! Don't let that frequency lock onto your core signature!
Fantastic. We avoided bandits and surface-dwellers only to attract the attention of a geological nightmare. Let's go inside before the hull peels apart.
The harmonic reading… it's not random. It's a pattern. A calling. If the Silencing was a command, this is the… response.
(Comms breaking apart) W-what is that?! My crystals are bleeding sound! The charts are lies! Don't let anyone know! Don't tell the Orders what's down here!

A beam of solidified sound, visible as twisting light, lances up from the Lattice. It doesn't strike your ship—it envelops it, humming with ancient intent. The Groundless Movement's warnings about hidden truths beneath the sky feel terrifyingly literal.
It's not attacking… it's *examining* us. Like we're a wrong note in its song.
Or a note that has been silent for too long. This is the discovery we feared. The truth that unmade the world.

line.dialogue: The ancient resonance holds your ship in a field of pure vibration. It seeks something—a specific frequency, a memory, a proof of identity. To break free, you must answer.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch out in terraced layers, their vibrant green a stark contrast to the shimmering, sound-reactive Lattice far below. Wind whispers through the rows of sky-rice, creating a gentle, rhythmic susurrus.
This peace… it feels earned. A fragile thing, built on the silence after the great noise.
Built on ignorance, more like. They farm their little patch and pretend the Lattice isn't down there, humming with whatever killed the old world.
A practical approach. Stability is precious. We should rest while we can.
Rest? Look! Someone's waving us over from that irrigation hut. Maybe they need help!
You're the ones with the Resonance ship, right? The newcomers? From that day you landed, folks have been talking.

There's a story here. An old one. About a ship that vanished into the Lattice mists near our gardens, generations back. The 'Echo.' Some say on quiet nights, you can still hear its crystal resonator… crying.
A lost song, trapped? Who would believe such a tale could linger for so long?

lines_after.dialogue: I believe it! A ghost ship! We have to find it!
Or it's a fairy tale to scare children and sell ale to gullible travelers.
Believe what you want. But old Mani, the monk who tends the wind-chime shrine… he's been listening for it. He doesn't look like he's smiling happily anymore.

You live near each other in this floating city, yet you hear nothing but the wind and your own thoughts. I'm happy to hear visitors… though I fear what brings you.
We were told you listen for the Echo. The lost ship.
I do. Its resonance is… wrong. A fracture in the world's song. My Order says to record, not to intervene. But this… it feels like a wound.
A dangerous discovery. If the Tonal Orders haven't charted it, there's a reason. It could be a navigational hazard.
Or it's a ship in trouble! There's no one else looking for it, right? Just us!
And a monk having a crisis of conscience. Lovely. So you've actually heard this 'Echo'?
Not with ears. With the shards. A dissonant pulse, deep below the western terrace, where the Lattice currents are treacherous. It does not belong.

lines_after.dialogue: A sound that doesn't belong… a life out of tune with the Lattice.
Precisely. To live is to resonate in harmony or discord. This is a sustained, painful discord.
Then we have to go down there! We can't just leave it!

No! This is the truth they buried! The Lost Ship, the *Resonance's Requiem*... its final crash seeded this place with its dying song!
I can't keep up with what you're saying! Is this the ship's ghost or a weapon?!
It's a data-corruption event. A resonant memory so traumatic it's physically rewriting the local Lattice structure. We're standing inside a scream.
The entire terrace section is destabilizing. If that primary support crystal shatters, this whole garden plate shears off the city.
The pilot. She's not attacking. She's *trapped*. Re-living the moment the false charts led her into a harmonic dead zone. Her panic is resonating through the crystals she crashed into.
The Tonal Orders... they scuttled the investigation. Said she was a rogue Singer. But we Listeners... we heard the truth in the static. And now it's awake.

lines_after.dialogue: The central crystal, the heart of the memory, pulses like a dying star. The image of the ship solidifies, superimposed over the crumbling garden. A choice must be made: silence the memory or set it free.
We don't get to bury this again. But we can't let it destroy the present.
So we give her a proper finale. One last, clear note.

Or it's just tired of holding up another floating rock full of people terrified of falling. He's right! The Tonal Orders charge a fortune just for the charts to get here.
Forget the charts! Look at this place! It's my dream job to find spots like this. Peace, food, no one trying to kill us...

We heard about the echoes in the channels. The guy in the condo next door always complains about noise, too. What's really down there?
Direct! I admire that. A local farmer, Old Kanya. She's... experimenting. Trying to grow a new crystal graft for her son's leg. A resonant prosthetic. It's making unstable frequencies.
Unstable resonance near the city's foundation? That's dangerously irresponsible.
But she's trying to help her son! We have to see!

Indeed. But her methods are crude. I have a calibrated crystal core that could stabilize her work. A bargain, for you. Or... you could report her to the Tonal Order enforcers. They'd pay a finder's fee.

lines_before.dialogue: The main chamber of the Tonal Archives falls into a profound silence. The air grows heavy with the scent of old vellum and ozone. Pichit's fingers trace the forbidden sigils in the ancient codex.
They've hidden entire continents down there. Safe routes my foot—these are cages. We have to tell people.
And be branded heretics? The Orders control the food, the water, the very air between islands. Your idealism is a death sentence.
She's right. This isn't just data. It's a weapon. If we're wrong about the intent behind these redactions...
The silence in these records... it's deliberate. A shaped void. Could you say that again, please, Malee? About the food supply?
Ah, diligent researchers! Finding everything you need? The Archives are a marvel, aren't they? So... orderly.
We're fine. Do you wanna try it? Reading between the lines of your guild's 'complete' records?
The Trade Negotiator's smile doesn't reach his eyes. His gaze lingers on the open codex. From the shadows of a nearby pillar, a Skycity Resident watches, wringing their hands.

lines_after.dialogue: Please... please translate that for me. The old script. My grandmother... she used to hum those lost tones. They said she was Groundless.
Wonderful. Now we have an audience. Just what we needed.
No. This is what we needed. A connection. The silence in the book... and the silence forced on the people.
A low, harmonic alarm begins to pulse through the Archives. The crystal lattices in the walls glow with a faint, angry light.

line.dialogue: The security resonance is activating. The Negotiator blocks the main exit, his friendly pretense gone. The Resident looks at you with desperate hope.

lines_before.dialogue: Chaos reigns in the sacred silence. Shattered crystal dust hangs in the air, catching the alarm's pulse. The Negotiator shouts orders to unseen guards. The Resident clutches a recovered fragment of song.
You've broken the First Accord! You drown us all in noise! Seize them!
Pichit, think! This is a sanctioned archive! What about tomorrow? What happens when they come for our ship, our homes?
Tomorrow doesn't exist if we live in a lie today! Is it real? Is their 'protection' real, or just a cage made of pretty sounds?
Oh, it's a cage. A very profitable, very stable cage. And we just rattled the bars. Loudly.
The tone... it's a calling. For the ones below. The Groundless. It says... 'the Lattice sings for all.'
That's it. The real crime wasn't the Silencing. It was the theft of the song. They took a world's voice and sold it back in pieces.

The central archive crystal, the Master Index, begins to resonate in sympathy with the recovered tone. A deep, fundamental frequency vibrates through the floor, through your bones. The true history of the world threatens to sound.

lines_after.dialogue: Stop it! You'll destabilize the city anchors! You'll kill us all!
No. We're finally listening. Please translate that for me, world. Show us what's real.
The Master Crystal flashes. Not with alarm, but with revelation. For a blinding second, perfect, uncharted harmonic pathways through the Lattice unfold in the air—a map of true freedom.
Then, with a sound like a held breath released, the crystal goes dark. The knowledge is gone from sight, but not from memory. The Archives are forever changed.

line.dialogue: The revealed truth is ephemeral. The Orders' guards are at the door. You hold a fragment of the true song, and the fate of the Groundless movement hangs on your next action.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim stretch out in terraced layers of gold and green, wheat stalks whispering in the wind like a slow, breathing sea. Water channels sing a gentle, percussive trickle down the stone tiers.
The rhythm here... it's almost like a lullaby the Lattice itself composed. Can I take a break for a moment? Just to listen?
A break? Pichit, we just got here! Look at those cloud-berries! I bet they're ripe!
Enjoy the pastoral fantasy. The moment we stop moving is the moment something finds us. The Silencing didn't leave many quiet corners.
Malee has a point. This tranquility is... statistically anomalous for an edge-settlement. We should remain observant.
A figure emerges from between the wheat rows—a woman clad in patched leather and crystal-dusted goggles. She eyes the party with sharp suspicion. the Surface scavenger
City-folk. Your ship's resonance is too clean. What do you want with my gardens? I have no one to help me up here, and I prefer it that way.
We mean no harm. We're just... travelers. Can I ask what you're listening for?

lines_after.dialogue: Listening? I'm surviving. The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for maps to the safe frequencies below. I hunt for the open ones—the natural harmonics the Lattice doesn't reject.
An unlicensed frequency hunter. How quaintly illegal.
Illegal is a city word. Down on the surface, it's just life. I found a cluster. Strong, clear resonance. Could be a new stable route. But my resonator crystal is cracked.
She holds up a palm-sized crystal, a hairline fracture glowing with a faint, erratic light.

The structural integrity of these old supports is concerning. And that vibration... it's not on any standard Tonal chart.
Standard charts are for people who love paying. You need to love yourself enough to find your own way. This pulse... it's pure. Untouched.
It's not just a frequency. It feels... intentional. Like a memory the Lattice is holding.
Or a very effective trap. Love yourself by not getting crystallized, Chanida.

The staircase opens into a small, natural cavern. In its center, a cluster of raw Lattice-crystals pulses in time with the hum, projecting a shimmering, three-dimensional pattern of intersecting lines into the air—a map.
There! The Open Frequency Map! It's real! Routes even the Orders don't know!

lines_before.dialogue: In the quietude of the gardens, the party catches their breath. The distant hum of the city's crystal resonators is a faint, steady baseline beneath the rustling of high-altitude wheat.
The silence here... it's not empty. It's layered. Like a memory waiting to be remembered.
Or a trap waiting to be sprung. That scavenger wasn't just being charitable. He gave us a map to get rid of us, or worse, to lead us into a sky pirate's net.
But the frequencies on this map! They're... open. Uncharted. Not controlled by the Tonal Orders. This could change everything!
Or get us permanently silenced. Navigating without sanctioned charts is what got the Listeners exiled. We need to be cautious.
Cautious, yes. But Arthit, this knowledge... it's like we're about to graduate from being passengers to becoming navigators of our own fate.
A sudden, sharp *CRACK* echoes from the lower terraces—not the sound of breaking crystal, but of a heavy door being slammed shut with violent force.
Speak of the devils. The guy in the condo next door always closes his door loudly. Or in this case, the sky pirate on the terrace below.

It belongs to anyone brave enough to use it!

acts.title: The Price of an Open Sky

lines_before.dialogue: Tension vibrates in the air, thicker than the garden's humidity. The pirates' hands hover near their makeshift sonic weapons.
Well? The price is the same, no matter how you pay. The map. Or we take it from the Lattice after it's done with you.
This is escalating beyond a simple theft. That map could help so many people... but not if it's hoarded by another monopoly.
Oh, wonderful. So our options are: get robbed by criminals or become martyrs for the greater good. I hate moral calculus.
It's not just a map. It's a key. To a world not controlled by the Orders. A world where anyone can listen... and sing.
He's right! This is worth fighting for! It's really worth seeing—what's on the other side of their control!
Last chance. The hard way, then. Crew, tune to shatter!
The pirates raise jagged resonator stones. A dissonant, painful whine begins to build, making the very leaves of the crops shudder.

lines_after.dialogue: In the ringing silence that follows the clash, the gardens are a tableau of consequences. Wilted crops, humming crystal shards, and the heavy weight of choice.
The sky is open... but every freedom has its cost. We just decided what ours was.
And I suppose you wish us good luck, too, dealing with what comes next? The Orders will have felt that resonance burst.
Then we don't have much time. The map is ours. Let's use it before the price gets any higher.

line.dialogue: The immediate threat is neutralized, but the map's true power—and danger—is now undeniable. How do you proceed with your hard-won prize?

Look at those colors! What kind of resonance do you think makes that? What style do you prefer, Pichit? The deep blues or the sharp, shivering whites?
I prefer the silence between the notes. The Listeners say the lattice's true song is in the pauses.
Poetic. Meanwhile, the Tonal Orders charge a fortune for the charts that keep us from shattering on it. Anywhere you like for a mis-tuned frequency. Anywhere.
Keep your voices low. The platform's dampeners are old. We're here to scavenge, not to philosophize.
You're the ones looking for the lost ship fragments? The 'Echo'? Why are you doing this to me? Asking me to guide you out here...
Why are you treating us like this? We paid you. Just point to the sector where the resonance shards fell.
Fine. Northwest quadrant. But the lattice there is... unstable. It whispers.

Got it! Are you sure this is all from one ship? It's scattered everywhere...
It was a Resonance Ship. When it broke, its tuning crystal exploded. I know. I've seen the reports.
There's a pattern to the dispersion... but I don't know where to begin deciphering it.

Sky pirates. We have no quarrel. We just need a few pieces for study.

For a price. Or for a fight. You heard that, didn't you? The lattice's getting antsy.

lines_before.dialogue: The resonance ship *Echo of Dawn* glides silently through the thin air, its crystal resonators humming a low, steady tone that parts the shimmering Lattice below like water. The deck is cool, the wind carrying the scent of ozone and distant rain.
Look at it... the Lattice doesn't just respond to sound. It *remembers*. Every note our ship sings is absorbed, becoming part of its eternal song.
And we're just scratching the surface! I bet if we pushed the harmonics, we could find paths the Tonal Orders haven't even charted! It works really well, this ship!
Easy for you to say. You're not the one who has to recalibrate the resonator arrays every time you get a 'brilliant' idea. He complains a lot! Every little vibration out of tune.
A valid concern, Malee. Uncharted frequencies could destabilize our crystal integrity. The manuals are clear...
Manuals written by the Orders! They're keeping secrets, I'm telling you!
From the starboard observation rail, the Listener Monk turns, his simple robes fluttering. His eyes are fixed not on the Lattice, but on a faint, discordant shimmer far to the east.
Your friend's zeal is... noticeable. But she is not entirely wrong. There are songs in the Lattice that the Orders do not teach. Songs of loss.

lines_after.dialogue: Ah, discussing navigation? A fascinating, if *specialized*, field. Best left to the experts, I always say. Less chance of... mishaps.
The Trade Negotiator approaches, his smile polished and unreadable. He follows the Monk's gaze to the distant shimmer.
Pay no mind to old echoes, friends. The Drift is full of phantom frequencies. Some cargoes are best left where they lie, if you catch my meaning. I'm really hurt you'd think I'd steer you wrong!
What cargo?
The Merchant's smile doesn't falter, but his eyes grow guarded.

lines_before.dialogue: The party chose to press the Merchant. After some tense conversation and implied threats about his contract, he reluctantly divulges a location: the last known coordinates of the *Argent Whisper*, a resonance ship lost decades ago. Its 'echo' still sometimes bleeds into the Drift.

Guided by the Monk's attuned ears, the *Echo of Dawn* alters course. The ambient hum of the ship deepens, taking on a melancholic, minor key as they approach the coordinates. The Lattice here is murky, swirling with faint, grayish light.
Readings are... anomalous. The resonance field is stable, but there's a persistent sub-harmonic. It's nice and peaceful, but it's a false peace. Like the calm before a storm.
Great. So we're sailing into a acoustic ghost story. Who is this guy, anyway, this lost captain? Another fool who thought he knew better than the charts?
His name was Kiet. He was a seeker. Not a fool. He believed the Lattice could be communed with, not just commanded. He was a nice person, by all accounts. Too curious for his own good.
A Singer! He had to be! The Orders wouldn't lose a regular ship this completely.

A sudden, sharp harmonic pierces the ship's ambient tone. The crystal viewports flicker. For a split second, the swirling gray light outside coalesces into the faint, translucent outline of another ship's prow, passing silently through their own.
Did you see...?
On the main resonator display, a phantom signal solidifies—not a ship's ID, but a simple, looping melodic phrase. A distress call. Or a warning.

lines_after.dialogue: I told you! Phantom frequencies! This is bad for business. We should leave. Now.
That melody... it is not a standard distress pattern. It is a personal motif. A signature. Captain Kiet is... introducing himself.

lines_before.dialogue: At the Spire's very apex, the world falls away. Above, the floating city glimmers. Below, the infinite, shimmering Lattice stretches to the horizon. The harmonic tone is a pure, clarifying force.

I stand at the center of the world's song, holding a note that was not meant to be sung. I don't feel the same as before we climbed. The harmony is more complex now. And more fragile.

Most of it's junk. But that... (points to a partially buried resonator array) That might sing again with some work.
The structural integrity is questionable. And what do your parents do, Chanida, to make you so comfortable crawling into unstable wrecks?
Salvagers, like me! They'd say this prize is worth the risk. I'll take very good care of it once it's ours.
Wait. Listen. Beneath the clanging... a purity tone. Uncorrupted.
A figure in ochre robes steps from behind a crystal column, hands raised in a gesture of peace. It's a Listener monk, their face etched with worry.
Please, you must cease. This place... it is not for taking. The Lattice here hums a warning. A disharmony that could fracture everything.

The charts are silent on truths we have... buried. My order studies the natural song. Here, the song is becoming a scream.
Convenient. A monk shows up just as we find valuable things. What's your real angle?

He hides among the compressor stacks. But listen... the Lattice's song here is wrong. A grinding dissonance beneath the scrapyard's noise. I didn't catch what you said earlier, Pichit, about the Silencing. Could it be... returning?
A systemic resonance collapse? The historical records are fragmented, but the acoustic profiles...
Great. So the world might end, and we're chasing a bandit who probably lost his phone and his last brain cell in the same bet.
The truth often hides in what we fail to hear. Lead us to him, Monk. We must piece this together before the Order silences it all.
A shriek of tearing metal echoes, followed by a rough laugh from the gantries above.

lines_after.dialogue: The Sky Pirate drops to a lower catwalk, a resonator pistol humming in his grip. The Monk steps back, conflicted.

Tell us everything! Now!

They're here. They've come to reclaim the knowledge, to bury the warning. I now know... my order has been complicit. We listened, but we never spoke.
Their ship is priming its dampeners. They intend to acoustically stun the entire area and take us all.
Of course. The bureaucratic solution: erase the problem and the witnesses. I told you this was a bad idea.
My ship's a wreck, but the old compressor array... hit it with that dying frequency, and the feedback might just scramble their systems. It's the best way. Also the only way.

Fun. Right. The Tonal Orders charge a fortune for these 'safe' charts, and all we get is a headache. Our captain left home in a hurry with these coordinates. I doubt he paid full price.
Caution is advised. These interference patterns aren't on any standard nav-log. Pichit, are you ready to go back home yet? This route feels... uncharted.
Home is a direction, not a place on these maps. The Lattice is speaking. We just need to learn how to listen past the charts.

Told you. 'Safe' is a relative term when you're skimming the world's scar.

Romantic. They just want to pick our bones. And don't make me cry! I paid good coin for the cargo in the hold.
Hostile signatures are converging. Our defensive harmonics are weak. I sprained my ankle once trying to run on a shifting deck. This feels similar—a bad footing.

Cut yer drone, city-slickers! We're comin' aboard for a chat. My girlfriend is jealous of quiet ships—means they got secrets worth takin'.
Violence is just another form of dissonance. But even a warning note can be struck with force.
Please, don't fight! They'll scuttle the ship! We'll all fall!

You navigate the static. You must hear it too. The Lattice is sick here. This isn't a place for piracy. It's a tomb tuning itself.

A song left in the stones... a memory of the Lattice's purer voice, before the Silencing. We should listen.

lines_before.dialogue: The Hanging Gardens of Mae Rim are a sanctuary of green. Tiered terraces cascade down the skycity's edge, their crops swaying in a gentle, rhythmic wind. Water channels hum with quiet melodies. The air smells of damp earth and blooming night-flowers. The party has stopped here to rest, the peace a stark contrast to their usual travels.
I could get used to this. No ship's hum, no Lattice static. Just... wind. And that weird, quiet ringing.
That 'weird ringing' is probably a cracked irrigation pipe. Don't get too comfortable. Places this quiet usually have something to hide.
The soil composition on these upper tiers is remarkable. Stable, yet responsive. A perfect place to recuperate. We should be safe here.
Safe, perhaps. But listen. The wind through the barley... it's not a random sound. It's phrasing. Like a breath held, then released.
You lot look like travelers. You're gonna be sorry if you're planning to head towards the western spurs after dark.
Why? What's out there?

Nothing good. Sounds that shouldn't be there. Like a ship's resonator, but... broken. Stuck on one awful note. Some say it's the echo of the *Amaranth*, a Resonance ship that vanished cycles ago. Could you tell me how to get to the Dusit Hotel? I've... I've got family coming in from another skycity and I need to meet them there. It's safer in the core.

lines_after.dialogue: A lost ship's echo? Sounds like a fantastic way to get ourselves killed chasing a ghost story.
A persistent sonic anomaly could indicate a destabilized Lattice zone. It *is* a legitimate hazard.
A broken note, stuck... That's not an echo. That's a wound. I have something to tell you. I've been hearing a dissonance in the garden's song since we arrived. It's coming from the west.
Well, we're not gonna just sit here and listen to it ache! Let's go find out what it is!

lines_before.dialogue: The party finds a Listener Monk in a small stone shrine carved into the garden's cliff face. He is meticulously tuning a set of crystal chimes, his movements precise but tense. The dissonant hum from the west is a faint, throbbing bass note here.

You hear it too. The scar in the song. I am... sorry. We have been monitoring it. We have to do something, but my Order forbids direct intervention. It is a 'natural phenomenon' to be studied, not silenced.
Let me guess. Studying it involves a lot of note-taking and not a lot of actually helping the people who have to listen to it every night.
It's not natural. It's mechanical. A resonator crystal, shattered but still powered. It's in pain.

You perceive deeply. You are right. It is the *Amaranth*'s primary resonator. The ship itself is gone, swallowed. But its heart... its heart is stuck there, screaming. I was part of the survey team that found the wreckage. We only recovered the log. The Captain's final entry... he loved it. The silence of the deep Lattice. He loved it!! And then it took him.
A feedback loop from a damaged crystal could theoretically propagate indefinitely, creating a permanent zone of auditory and potentially physical instability. You can put your hand down now.

lines_after.dialogue: I am sorry because I transcribed that log. I heard the Captain's love turn to terror in his voice. And my Order sealed the record. Said it would 'cause panic.' The truth is buried in our archives while that crystal weeps.
That's horrible! We can't just leave it like that!
Great. So we're dealing with a haunted crystal and a cover-up. My favorite.
The truth is a frequency, not a document. It's vibrating in the air right now. We can either listen to the Order, or we can listen to the song.

That's the echo! The lost ship's final frequency! We're close. Give it to me! Let me follow it to the source!
Chanida, wait. We finished deciphering the Listener's data, but this resonance is unstable. Pushing forward blind is... unwise.
Arthit is right, but the truth is down there. The Monk's records... I went to bed late last night piecing them together. The Tonal Orders didn't just lose that ship. They silenced it.
You... you shouldn't have that knowledge.
What are you saying? The Orders protect us!
They protect their monopoly. That ship found a new, pure resonance path. A threat to their charts. So they scuttled it, and buried the song.

Look at that refraction... It's really worth seeing! The Lattice isn't just responding to our ship's tone—it's remembering something older.
Remembering how to swallow ships whole, probably. Your philosophical wonder doesn't pay for repairs when we hit a dissonance pocket.
Forget the repairs! Look at the scope! A frequency spike, way off the Tonal charts. It's pulsing. A ghost signal.

But what if it's the Echo? The lost ship from the subplot? I really wonder... What if we're the first to find it in decades?

Catastrophic resonance cascade. The Lattice solidifies around us. We become the next echo. Those are the top three.

(Over the comms, voice panicked) It's the Enforcers! They monitored the ghost signal! You have to run! They'll scrap your ship and silence your crew!
They're broadcasting a lattice-lock frequency. If it syncs, our resonator will shut down. We'll be dead in the sky. I can't make it back to the helm if they jam us!
Let them try! What kind of fight do you prefer? Straight through, or messy? Their big ships can't turn like we can!
Oh, it's not scary at all! Just three-to-one odds against the world's monopoly on violent acoustics. What could go wrong?
The vortex the ghost pointed to—it's a chaotic frequency zone. Orders' charts avoid it. My... less official maps say it's passable, for a singer. It's a graduate-level course in not dying.
We hold the echo's truth. A truth they've buried. We don't just run. We choose the path they fear. We make the Lattice sing for *us*.

The lead Enforcer ship fires a warning shot—a concentrated sonic pulse that shears through a mast. The time for debate is over. The storm of the chaotic zone churns ahead, the orderly fleet of the Orders closes behind.

line.dialogue: The path splits. The chaotic vortex promises obscurity but unimaginable peril. The Enforcer fleet offers a brutal, direct confrontation. You're the ones asking about the Lost Ship? I went to bed late last night, couldn't sleep. Kept thinking about it. My granddad said its resonance still drifts out there, like a ghost in the crystal.
A ghost in the crystal... or a pattern the Orders chose to forget. Why would a fully-charted vessel just vanish?
Forgive the interruption. I am Kavi. Some songs are silenced not by the Lattice, but by those who fear what they might reveal.

What you feel in your bones is probably tetanus. This is a scrap heap. The only 'history' here is how many credits we'll lose on fuel.
We should proceed with caution. The scavengers here don't take kindly to outsiders poking around. Could you tell me how to get to the foreman's shack? A proper introduction might smooth our way.

Every broken ship has a final note in its song. We just need to listen. Chanida's right. I have something to tell you all... I've been hearing a fragment of melody here for weeks. It doesn't match any known ship signature.
Hey! You lot lost? This ain't a tourist dock.
We're looking for a ship. An old one. Maybe... a lost one?
They're all lost 'til we find 'em. What's it to you?

lines_after.dialogue: We seek understanding, not salvage. The song it left behind... it's incomplete.
Song, eh? You one of those Listeners? Fine. There's a hull in Sector Gamma. Been there years. Makes the lattice weep if you get too close. Even the breakers won't touch it.
The scavenger points a grimy finger toward a canyon of twisted metal. A low, dissonant hum seems to emanate from that direction, felt more than heard.

I can smell it... ozone and old roses. I smelled perfume like that once, in my grandmother's trunk. It's coming from the ship.
Not a smell... a memory resonance. The ship is holding onto a moment. Chanida, you're connecting to it. I'm the luckiest person in the world to have a crew that senses what others miss.

lines_after.dialogue: The 'Amaranth's Lament'. A private vessel lost just before The Silencing. Its final song is a closed loop of grief. I have studied it for years, but... the Order says to observe, not to intervene.

It is not a scream. It is a question. Repeated. I can smell the perfume too, you know. Lilac and ionized air. It asks 'Where are you?'
The hull shudders, not physically, but in the resonant layer. A ghostly image flickers by the entry hatch—a woman in pre-Silencing attire, looking back, her form woven from light and sound.

It's not just a sound. It's a memory. The ship is remembering its final moments. We're standing right in front of a frozen scream.

Listen... beneath the steady tone. There are layers. Faint cries, echoes of the old world, trapped in the crystal. This place is a memory.

Malee gestures to a group of the villagers tending to hydroponic vines. Their movements are slow, deliberate, and utterly silent.

Why are you doing this to me? Why are you treating me like this? We're just resting!
